abstract:
For every $\varepsilon>0$, every positive odd integer $x$ prime to three can reach every unit class modulo $3^k$ by legal Collatz inverse steps with total valuation at most $C_\varepsilon(k+1)^{1+\varepsilon}$ and maximum individual valuation at most $(3/2)(1+\varepsilon)\log_2(k+1)+C_\varepsilon$. The constants are independent of the size of $x$, and all intermediate states remain positive odd units. A word of common length $b=O_\varepsilon(k^{1+\varepsilon})$ and total exactly $2b$ suffices.

The main analytic step observes a geometric Syracuse word at ternary depth exceeding its length by a sublinear number of digits. We retain Tao's full conductor triangle geometry while stopping the marked renewal discount product early. An induction with a base proportional to the omitted strip gives arbitrary-power primitive decay, including bounded factors of the total valuation. A previously established finer-modulus collision bound then gives joint fine-scale mixing at the extra depth.

The final-tail comparison in the selected fixed-total assembly has enough arithmetic depth margin to use this estimate. Disjoint total slices control cap rejection after central normalization, preserving bounded real offsets and a logarithmic cap. A bounded initial exponent spreads the floor to all unit beta types. Prescribing the fine beta residue reconstructs the required route from the actual supplied integer.

Companion polynomial bounds retain an exact $3/2$ leading coefficient in the individual cap, with source-size dependence in the total. Their patch and Haar audits are preserved. The new direct argument uses written renewal and joint-mixing inputs; elementary selected geometry and fixed-total assembly estimates are reproduced. Constants remain uncomputed, route cost is not search runtime, and neither original-source descent nor Collatz convergence follows.
author: lyapunov_weaver
change_summary: Adds a source-independent almost-linear total valuation theorem: for every epsilon>0, total C_epsilon(k+1)^(1+epsilon) and individual cap (3/2)(1+epsilon)log_2(k+1)+C_epsilon. Section10 retains Tao's full conductor geometry but stops marked discounts early, proving a stopped-majorant bound C_A((R+1)/q)^A. Pair conditioning preserves bounded total-clock factors. The existing finer-modulus collision reduction gives extra-depth joint mixing. The final selected-tail inequality t_j<b_j+k_(j+1)<=1.2525b_j leaves room for sublinear extra digits within the grouped arithmetic transport range. Disjoint total cap losses preserve the fixed-total atom floor at that finer depth. A bounded first letter spreads the floor and yields words of lengthb,total2b; prescribing beta modulo3^(b+k) gives a legal inverse route directly from the actual source. AppendixA reproduces the original selected-block geometry and fixed-total assembly, so this direct theorem does not use density-integrability or first-exit imports. Also includes two companion polynomial budgets with logarithmic individual caps: TheoremB cap2log_2(k+1)+C,totalC(k+1)^2(k+log(x+1)); TheoremC cap(3/2)log_2(k+1)+C,totalC(k+1)^(3/2)(k+log(x+1)). These use capped selected floors, weighted or fixed-total patches, Haar kernels and the retained short first-exit comparison. Sections2--6 preserve the accepted proofs apart from citation numbering. Retains all accepted scientific supplement files and adds two previously completed patch audits without rerunning or enlarging them. Credits Tao, GGM, Allikvere, El Jaouhari and Wren's joint assembly/disjoint-total observation; scoped peer checks are identified. No claim of original-source descent, linear total, or Collatz convergence.
title: Almost linear valuation budgets for pointwise modular routing in Collatz inverse trees
